Chapter 2 — Configuration

Powerful control without complexity

One of the defining principles of Panels DCC is that everything is configured visually. There is no requirement to write scripts, edit configuration files, or understand complex command structures. If you can drag, drop, and click, you can build and operate a sophisticated DCC layout.

From trains and accessories to full signalling-style panels, configuration happens directly in the interface, with immediate visual feedback.

Before you create an account or subscription

Cloud-based design and your account work together with PanelsDCC Connect and PanelsDCC Control on your Raspberry Pi. Complete Getting started (install software, Wi‑Fi, Connect, first train, and your PanelsDCC account) before you rely on a subscription.

That means your command station is detected and controllable, and Control shows a healthy connection so you can drive at least one locomotive and one accessory as expected.

Trains

Panels DCC draws on an extensive UK locomotive library, allowing new trains to be added simply by typing a description. Images and core details are loaded instantly, removing the need for manual data entry or hunting for reference material.

For sound-fitted locomotives, Panels DCC includes a growing library of DCC function maps. Instead of remembering function numbers, you control features through clear, recognisable icons — lights look like lights, horns look like horns.

Functions and Function Maps — create custom maps, upload icons, add functions to maps, and reorder so favourites appear first.

Unlike many systems, Panels DCC also lets you:

  • Create your own custom functions and function maps
  • Upload and assign your own icons to functions and maps
  • Add functions to existing maps
  • Reorder functions so your favourites appear first

This means the control interface adapts to how you drive, not the other way around.

Image/Video: Train config

Accessories

Accessory configuration in Panels DCC is just as visual as train control.

We provide a growing set of pre-built animated accessories, including:

  • Digital colour-light signals
  • Semaphore signals with realistic movement
  • Turnouts and other layout elements

These aren't abstract symbols — they are designed to look like the real thing, making the state of the layout immediately obvious during operation.

Macros — group accessories and routes for repeatable operation where your layout supports it.

You can also define your own accessories, using non-animated visuals that change automatically based on state.

Image/Video: Animated Accessories

Panels

Panels are where your diagram meets your layout: you build them visually in the panel editor.

Drag elements into place to match your trackwork and operating scheme. Then configure each element — for example, add signals to sections so the panel reflects how you run trains.

Link those elements to accessories you have already defined, or create and configure a new accessory without leaving the panel editor when something is missing. The panel stays the centre of the work: layout, signals, and accessories stay connected in one place.
